# Compiled reverse Core

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/reverse-core.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

After acceptance, the kernel compiles every reverse site of a checked module into Core of its own. A site is a pullback in either mode, a differential or the reverse pass of a tape. The forward Core at the site binds the input point r₀ and the images rᵢ = mᵢ(rᵢ₋₁) along the maps m₁, …, m_k of the site. A generated backward function pulls the seed back along m_k, …, m₁: a declared map by its Jacobian table, any other map value by the runtime reverse pass. The ledger of the compilation lists every site with its generated function. The theorems below concern the checked Core and the kernel evaluator, not the generated text or native code.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/reverse-core.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/reverse-core.toml).

<a id="reverse-core.backward.saved"></a>

## Saved backward Core

- Property: `reverse-core.backward.saved`
- Subject: `Core.Reverse.Entry.generated`
- Rule: [Smooth affine geometry and reverse pullbacks](../verification.md#smooth-affine-geometry-and-reverse-pullbacks)

Let a saved site have the step programs m₁, …, m_k, which compose. Call its generated backward function on one program per opaque step, the input point r₀, saved points r₁, …, r_k and a seed η, where each rᵢ has the coordinates of mᵢ(rᵢ₋₁). The call evaluates to the saved-mode pullback of η along m_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ m₁ at r₀. A seed that does not lie over r_k gives the failure value ⊥. This holds for every entry of a compiled module.

- Example: In the acceptance example, the site pullback(gAfterF, x, seed), with gAfterF = compose(g(), f()), saves f(3) = (3, 9) and g(3, 9) = 18. Its generated function pulls dt at 18 back to 12 dt at 3, and the seed dt at 17 gives the failure value.
- Run by: `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCore.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.saved_function_pullback`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.saved_function_foreign_seed`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCompiled.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compiled_saved_entry`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compiled_saved_entry_foreign_seed`
  - Premises:
    - for `saved_function_pullback` and `saved_function_foreign_seed`: the module declares the backward step of every map under the site's names (`StepsDeclared`), the map type of every declared step names two objects (`StepFormed`), the site has a step, and the activation binds the parameters of the generated function to the arguments
    - `compiled_saved_entry` and `compiled_saved_entry_foreign_seed` discharge these module premises for every entry of a compiled module
    - one program per opaque step
    - for the pullback: the programs compose (`Composable`) and the saved points satisfy the residual relation (`ResidualRel`)
    - for `saved_function_foreign_seed`: the residual relation, and a seed whose point is not that of the last saved point
    - for the compiled forms: the entry belongs to the ledger of a compiled module, its site saves, and the arguments of the call evaluate to the opaque programs, the points and the seed
  - Note: None of these theorems uses the chain rule. The proofs use the Jacobian table steps (`VastitasOracle.SmoothJacobian.jacobianStep_eq_of_output`) and the stepwise pullback, and `scripts/check_chain_rule_free.lean` checks this on the constants that each theorem uses. That consecutive steps share their objects is not proved, and no theorem needs it.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `acceptance_sites_compile_to_generated_backward_functions` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - `mutated_observations_change_the_native_result` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.ReverseCoreRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ReverseCoreRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: Observations 2 and 8 of the [acceptance example](../stage3-acceptance.md#acceptance-conditions) run compiled saved sites, the second with a seed over another point. The Rust test checks that the saved sites receive the images from the caller. `ReverseCoreRegression` compares every compiled site with its source site, failures included, and rejects forged backward functions.
- `bridge`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#623](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/623)
- `native`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)

## Recomputed backward Core and agreement of the policies

- Property: `reverse-core.backward.recomputed`
- Subject: `Core.Reverse.Entry.generated`
- Rule: [Smooth affine geometry and reverse pullbacks](../verification.md#smooth-affine-geometry-and-reverse-pullbacks)

Call the generated backward function of a recomputing site on one program per opaque step, the input point r₀ and a seed η, with programs that compose. It evaluates the images again and gives the recomputing pullback of η along m_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ m₁ at r₀. With saved points that are the images, the saved and the recomputing generated functions of a site have the same value. This holds for every entry of a compiled module.

- Example: pullback_recomputed(gAfterF, x, seed) evaluates f and g again in its generated function and agrees with the saved pullback. Along sq ∘ g ∘ f the recomputing function evaluates sq at its own forward point 18, so dt at 324 pulls back to 36 · 12 = 432 dt.
- Run by: `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCore.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.recomputed_function_pullback`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.saved_eq_recomputed`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCompiled.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compiled_recomputed_entry`
  - Premises:
    - for `recomputed_function_pullback` and `saved_eq_recomputed`: the module declares the forward step `smoothApply` and the backward step of every map under the site's names, the map type of every declared step names two objects, every declared step is a declaration with the derivative rule `morphism` (`MorphismsDeclared`), the site has a step, and the activations bind the parameters to the arguments
    - `compiled_recomputed_entry` discharges these module premises for every entry of a compiled module
    - one program per opaque step, and the programs compose
    - for `saved_eq_recomputed`: the saved points satisfy the residual relation, and both bodies evaluate; the theorem states that their values agree
    - for `compiled_recomputed_entry`: the entry belongs to the ledger of a compiled module, its site recomputes, and the arguments of the call evaluate to the opaque programs, the input point and the seed
  - Note: None of these theorems uses the chain rule. The proofs use `VastitasOracle.SmoothRuntime.pullback_saved_eq_recomputed` and the table steps, and `scripts/check_chain_rule_free.lean` checks this.

## Forward Core

- Property: `reverse-core.forward`
- Subject: `Core.Reverse.forwardLets`
- Rule: [Smooth affine geometry and reverse pullbacks](../verification.md#smooth-affine-geometry-and-reverse-pullbacks)

The forward Core of a site binds, one let per step and in application order, the evaluated images r₁ = m₁(r₀), …, r_k = m_k(r_{k-1}) of the input point. It evaluates to a value exactly when its body evaluates to that value with those points bound. The points satisfy the residual relation, and r_k has the coordinates of the primal value m_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ m₁ at r₀. The compiled Core of a site holds these lets after the input point.

- Example: At the site pullback(gAfterF, x, seed) of the acceptance example, the forward Core binds f(3) = (3, 9) and then g(3, 9) = 18 before it calls the generated function.
- Run by: `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCore.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.forwardLets_evaluates`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.forwardLets_primal`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCompiled.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compileSite_term`
  - Premises:
    - the module declares the forward step under the site's name as `smoothApply`; `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.entry_well_formed` discharges this for every entry of a compiled module
    - the map terms evaluate to the step programs and read no symbol at or above a bound, every bound symbol is at or above it, and the term of the previous point evaluates to the input point
    - for the primal value in `forwardLets_primal`: the site has a step
    - `compileSite_term` states the shape of the term that `compileSite` returns; it has no premise beyond the compilation of the site
  - Note: None of these theorems uses the chain rule.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `acceptance_sites_compile_to_generated_backward_functions` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.ReverseCoreRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ReverseCoreRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: Observation 2 of the [acceptance example](../stage3-acceptance.md#acceptance-conditions) reads the result of a site whose forward Core binds two images. `ReverseCoreRegression` rejects a site that passes the input point as an image.

## Meaning in coordinates

- Property: `reverse-core.meaning`
- Subject: `Core.Reverse.Entry.generated`
- Rule: [Smooth affine geometry and reverse pullbacks](../verification.md#smooth-affine-geometry-and-reverse-pullbacks)

Let the chain m_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ m₁ of the step programs be well typed from ℝⁿ to ℝᵐ, and let the seed η lie over its image of the input point x with m components. Then the generated backward function of a saved or a recomputing site evaluates to the covector at x whose components are cot of the composite map at x applied to η.

- Example: The compiled sites of stepwise pull dt at g(f(3)) = 18 back to 12 dt at 3, the derivative of g ∘ f(t) = 2t² at 3. The compiled differential of g(x, y) = x² + y at (1, 2) is (2, 1).
- Run by: `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCore.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.pullback_chain_cot`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.saved_function_cot`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCompiled.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compiled_saved_entry_cot`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compiled_recomputed_entry_cot`
  - Premises:
    - the premises of the saved or the recomputed backward Core without `Composable`, which the typing of the chain implies
    - the chain of the step programs is well typed from n to m
    - the seed lies over the chain's image of the input point and has m components
    - for a saved site: the saved points satisfy the residual relation
  - Note: These theorems use the chain rule `VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus.backward_eq_cot`, through `pullback_chain_cot`. The other properties of this file do not, which `scripts/check_chain_rule_free.lean` checks on constants. Component j of cot f x η is Σᵢ ηᵢ (∂ⱼ fᵢ)(x).
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - `mutated_observations_change_the_native_result` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
  - Note: Observations 1 and 18 of the [acceptance example](../stage3-acceptance.md#acceptance-conditions) read 12 dt and (2, 1) from compiled sites. The mutation test shows that a wrong result changes the native output.
- `bridge`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#623](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/623)
- `native`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: The theorems concern the Core that the kernel generates and the kernel evaluator. No claim states that the generated text or the compiled native code refines them. Tests run the native code.

<a id="reverse-core.sites"></a>

## Rewritten sites

- Property: `reverse-core.sites`
- Subject: `Core.Reverse.compileSite`
- Rule: [Smooth affine geometry and reverse pullbacks](../verification.md#smooth-affine-geometry-and-reverse-pullbacks)

The term that the compilation puts at a site and the source call evaluate to the same value. This holds for a pullback in either mode, for a differential, whose generated seed is the unit covector at the primal value, and for the reverse pass of a tape, direct or bound by a let. The maps that the derivative rules read from the map operand are its maps: its value is a composition tree whose leaves are the step programs.

- Example: In the Core module of the cotangent regression, each of the 45 sites, compiled on its own, evaluates to the value of its source site, failures included.
- Run by: [`VastitasKernel.ReverseCoreRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ReverseCoreRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCompiled.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compiled_site_evaluates`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.compileSite_term`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.resolve_factors`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCore.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.site_saved_core`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.site_recomputed_core`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.site_differential_core`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.site_saved_rewrite`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.site_recomputed_rewrite`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.site_differential_rewrite`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCore.site_tape_rewrite`
  - Premises:
    - for `compiled_site_evaluates`: the module keeps the bindings of the source declarations and holds every entry of the ledger (`EntryWellFormed`, which `entry_well_formed` proves for a compiled module)
    - for `compiled_site_evaluates` and `resolve_factors`: the let definitions in scope agree with the activation (`DefsAgree`), reading no symbol at or above the first symbol that the compilation binds
    - for `compiled_site_evaluates`: the map operand evaluates to a well-typed program, and the map, point and seed operands read no symbol at or above that symbol
    - for the local theorems (`site_*_core`, `site_*_rewrite`): the opaque terms and the point and seed terms evaluate, reading no symbol at or above a bound below the site's symbols, and the map operand's value is a composition tree of the step programs (`Factors`)
    - for the differential: the seed declaration is a `fiberVector` of the site's cotangent family, and that family has a variance
  - Note: `compiled_site_evaluates` states the property for the term that `compileSite` returns, the lets of the compound opaque leaves included. None of these theorems uses the chain rule, which `scripts/check_chain_rule_free.lean` checks.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasKernel.ReverseCoreRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ReverseCoreRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
    - `a_branch_chooses_the_map_of_a_reverse_pass` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - `a_tape_bound_by_let_compiles_and_a_tape_passed_to_a_function_keeps_its_routine` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
  - Note: `ReverseCoreRegression` evaluates every source site and its compiled Core. The Rust tests run sites whose map a branch chooses and sites on a tape bound by a let.

  - Issue: [#623](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/623)

<a id="reverse-core.validation"></a>

## Translation validation and public paths

- Property: `reverse-core.validation`
- Subject: `Core.Reverse.Compiled`
- Rule: [Smooth affine geometry and reverse pullbacks](../verification.md#smooth-affine-geometry-and-reverse-pullbacks)

A compilation stage holds its generated module and ledger exactly when compiling the source module again gives both. Every entry's generated function and declarations are found by their ids. Every entry is well formed: its site has a step, and every declared step names two objects and is a declaration with the derivative rule morphism. Its forward, backward and seed steps are declared under its names. On protocols 2-6, 7 and 8/9, consider every entry of a compiled module that the accepted certificate carries, or of the module that the pure emit path generates code from. A call of its generated function computes the pullback along the chain of the step programs passed as arguments, in its mode.

- Example: The 22 reverse calls of the acceptance program compile to 22 generated functions, numbered after the source functions and placed first. Each Jacobian step lies in a generated function.
- Run by: `acceptance_sites_compile_to_generated_backward_functions` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.IndexedReverseCore`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/IndexedReverseCore.lean): `VastitasOracle.IndexedReverseCore.validate_iff`, `VastitasOracle.IndexedReverseCore.compiled_entry_resolves`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothReverseCompiled.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.entry_well_formed`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.public_wire_entries`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.legacy_wire_entries`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.public_resource_entries`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothReverseCompiled.public_pure_entry_computes`
  - Premises:
    - for `compiled_entry_resolves` and `entry_well_formed`: the entry belongs to the ledger of a compilation stage (`Reverse.Compiled`) of a checked module
    - for `public_pure_entry_computes`: the request decodes to a program without a resource entry, and the emit path succeeds
    - `EntryComputes` keeps the premises on the arguments of a call: one program per opaque step, composable programs and, for a saved site, the residual relation of the saved points
  - Note: Validation is translation validation by recompilation, not an independent checker. None of these theorems uses the chain rule. That consecutive steps share their objects is not proved, and no theorem needs it. A pin covers the statement of a theorem, and a claim pins theorems and kernel definitions only. The pins of the public-path theorems therefore do not cover the oracle definitions `EntryComputes` and `EntryWellFormed`. Reviewers read those definitions with the theorems. That `Main.process` generates code from the compiled module of protocols 2-7 is read from `Main`, which the oracle does not import.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `acceptance_sites_compile_to_generated_backward_functions` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - `the_wire_cannot_name_the_compiled_declarations` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - `a_reverse_pass_through_an_object_outside_the_cotangent_domain_keeps_the_runtime_pass` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.ReverseCoreRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ReverseCoreRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: The Rust tests pin the shape of the compiled acceptance program, check that the wire cannot name the compiler's declarations, and run a site that keeps the runtime reverse pass. `ReverseCoreRegression` rejects forged ledgers, missing, extra and misowned generated functions, and sites left uncompiled.
- `bridge`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#623](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/623)
- `native`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: The theorems concern the Core that the kernel generates and the kernel evaluator. No claim states that the generated text or the compiled native code refines them. Tests run the native code.

<a id="reverse-core.steps"></a>

## Compiled steps

- Property: `reverse-core.steps`
- Subject: `cotangentJacobian`
- Rule: [Smooth affine geometry and reverse pullbacks](../verification.md#smooth-affine-geometry-and-reverse-pullbacks)

The backward step along a declared map m applies the Jacobian table of m, which the kernel computes from the exact map, to the seed. The table applied to a seed η at a point x is cot m x η. When the saved output point is the image of the input point, the table step is the pullback along m at the input point, for every seed. Every registry binding keeps the promise of its derivative rule, which the compilation reads.

- Example: The table step of g(x, y) = x² + y at (3, 9) pulls dt at 18 back to 6 dx + dy, and the table step of f(t) = (t, t²) at 3 pulls that back to 12 dt.
- Run by: `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothJacobian`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothJacobian.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothJacobian.transposeApply_jacobian`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothJacobian.jacobianStep_eq_of_output`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothJacobian.jacobianStep_eq`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothJacobian.registry_reverse_sound`
  - Premises:
    - for `jacobianStep_eq_of_output`: the coordinates of the saved output point are the image of the input point's coordinates under the map
    - for `jacobianStep_eq`: the output point is `applyPoint` of the map at the input point, and the mode is `saved`
  - Note: None of these theorems uses the chain rule.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `acceptance_sites_compile_to_generated_backward_functions` in [`tests/reverse_core.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/reverse_core.rs)
    - `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.ReverseCoreRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/ReverseCoreRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: The Rust test checks that every Jacobian step carries its table as a literal of rational polynomials. `ReverseCoreRegression` pins the generated function of one declared step and rejects a step along another declared map.
- `bridge`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#623](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/623)
- `native`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: The theorems concern the Core that the kernel generates and the kernel evaluator. No claim states that the generated text or the compiled native code refines them. Tests run the native code.
